title.narrative: Bridging Grant for AU Liaison Office - SECAM

description.narrative:
As part of SECAM’s aim to influence policies to promote the integral human development of citizens and communities across the continent, the AU liaison office was established in Addis Ababa in January 2015. This was part of Phase 3 of the Good Governance Project, funded through a consortium of CIDSE partners, led by Misereor and with CAFOD support. The liaison office aims to facilitate SECAM engagement at AU level, strengthening the voice of the Church on issues of concern for the continent, advocating for policy change and sharing relevant information with regional and national Bishops Conferences to facilitate advocacy.
In 2015 SECAM signed an MoU with African Union Commission and has since developed an advocacy strategic plan. Key activities have included hosting a Bishops trip seeking peace in Burundi, making submissions on natural resources management and silencing the guns, and coordinating closely with CPLOs for effective links between national and international advocacy.
In November 2016 the AU liaison office was closed at the same time as the third phase of the Good Governance Project came to an end. SECAM management sought a break between phase 3 and 4, while addressed various internal issues. Further project funding is awaiting the development of a new proposal as well as completion of project closure document and the clarification of outstanding issues from previous projects.
At a meeting on March 8th 2017 between Management teams of SECAM, Miseroer and CAFOD, issues with previous projects were deemed satisfactorily resolved (although still awaiting a review of final documentation) and it was agreed that a six-month bridging fund would be provided to SECAM from 1st April until 30th September 2017 aimed at: - Developing a proposal for Phase 4 of the Good Governance Project - Reopening the AU liaison office (from 1st March) - Developing a work-plan for SECAM and the AU liaison office around one of the priority issues identified by SECAM, namely migration
